ca_pacific_ocean_cliff.blurb: Pacific Ocean Cliff is one of the larger stone faces inside Sue-meg State Park, the former Patrick's Point State Park on the Redwood Coast. It looks out over the water, with wide views along the shoreline. There are eight routes in a mix of styles: three sport lines, two top-rope climbs, two trad routes and one aid route. Free grades run from 5.10 up to a single 5.13, so this is a wall for climbers already comfortable on harder terrain rather than a place to learn.

ca_johnny_cash_boulders.blurb: Johnny Cash Boulders is a pair of blocks about ten feet tall in Salt Point State Park, set among trees just above Highway 1. The sandstone is grainy and the blocks are oversized. There are eight problems, most of them between V1 and V3, with a few harder ones reaching V7. A long traverse on the bigger block gives a sustained pump over roughly twenty-five feet. Problems finish by dropping off the back rather than topping out.

ca_schoolboy_buttress.blurb: Schoolboy Buttress is a steep sport wall on Crystal Crag, above the Lake George parking area in the Mammoth Lakes basin. The faces are steep and broken up by overlapping roofs, so the climbing is sustained and physical. It has eight routes: seven sport and one trad. Grades start at 5.9 and run through 5.13, with most of the routes clustered between 5.10 and 5.11. It is best suited to climbers who already lead sport comfortably in the 5.10s.

ca_upper_shorty_crag.blurb: Upper Shorty Crag is a small crag on the hillside above the Echo Cove parking area, sitting higher than the lower crag beside it. Its raised base gives it better views than its size suggests. There are eight short climbs: six trad routes, one sport route and one top-rope problem. Grades run from very easy up to 5.10, with most routes in the 5.6 to 5.7 range, so it works for beginners learning to place gear as well as for climbers wanting a few quick laps. The routes are fairly new and should clean up with more traffic.

ca_two_trees_east.blurb: Two Trees East is a loose scatter of boulders, cracks and faces around the point where the Two Trees Trail ends, in Box Springs Mountain Reserve above Riverside. The climbs spread out in both directions and sit close to Box Springs Mountain Road. There are eight climbs: five trad routes, mostly low-grade with a single 5.9, and three boulder problems between V0 and V2. Rock quality swings from very good to crumbly, so test holds before pulling on them. The views over Riverside are good, and the hillside turns green after enough rain.
